title: Dispatch and drain Engram recovery turns before replaying queued prompts
outcome: TermAl automatically resolves Engram recovery_required responses and resumes each retained user or mailbox prompt exactly once.
acceptance: A deterministic host integration test rebinds a session with more than MAX_CONTROL_DELIVERY_EVENTS outstanding events, proves at least two recovery pages are consumed, and verifies the original prompt completes without user resubmission.

During recovery the UI reports a recoverable waiting state rather than 'Engram did not authorize this turn for runtime delivery', and queued submissions do not accumulate as indistinguishable ordinary retries.
TermAl drains every partial recovery page until the Engram control session is ready, preserving stable retry identity and never invoking the model provider before a valid grant and begin.

The original direct, queued, or mailbox prompt remains byte-for-byte unchanged and is dispatched exactly once after recovery; repeated wakeups do not duplicate, overwrite, or strand it, and cancellation remains available.
When Engram refuses an ordinary root turn with recovery_required, TermAl submits a purpose=recovery turn instead of retrying purpose=ordinary or reporting a terminal policy denial.
disposal_reason: Greg's turn-gate decisions (25 Sep, w-d5aa5056bbce) remove recovery turns together with the grant's context page. Engram no longer demands recovery turns, so TermAl needs no machinery to dispatch and drain them.
